channel.description: Latest articles from Andalusia Star News (andalusiastarnews.com)

item.title: LBW to Host SkillsUSA South District Competition
item.description: LBW Community College will host more than 350 high school competitors for the Alabama SkillsUSA South District workforce skills contest on Feb. 13, 2026, in Opp.

item.title: Covington County Losses in WWII: June-July 1944
item.description: Profiles five Covington County, Alabama servicemen killed in Europe June–July 1944, from D-Day landings to Operation Cobra, and where they now rest or are memorialized.

item.title: Opp City Council talks OHS Cheer and Rodeo
item.description: Opp council honors OHS cheer national champs, adjusts Rattlesnake Rodeo rain insurance hours, and transfers a utility right-of-way and pump duties to nearby owners.

item.title: ACC to abate nuisance properties
item.description: Andalusia council OKs nuisance property abatement and funds new police barricades at brief Tuesday meeting, targeting several addresses cited in complaints.

item.title: Pine Hills Storage Hub the largest of its kind
item.description: Covington County residents mobilize after learning months late about a proposed world-leading CO2 storage hub, as EPA stalls the project and lawmakers weigh a local ban.

item.title: Sheriff Candidate meet and greet to be held
item.description: Covington County voters can meet sheriff candidates at a Feb. 13, 6:30 p.m. FOP Lodge #19 event in Andalusia, aimed at open, non-debate conversations about their plans and policies.

item.title: When preserving local history becomes a family affair
item.description: How Emmitt Nix, Andalusia's “Picture Man,” and his son Joe use decades of photographs to document local Black history at the Three Notch Museum.

item.title: CCSCA students to compete for Thespy Awards
item.description: CCS Collaborative Arts theatre students earned six Superior ratings at the Alabama Thespian Festival, earning invitations to the 2026 International Thespian Festival and staging Cinderella Feb. 13–15.

item.title: Mia Baumgartner: A very distinguished young women
item.description: Covington County’s Mia Baumgartner, newly named 2026 Distinguished Young Woman of Alabama, prepares to compete nationally while championing literacy and community service.
